question: Can a benchmark of overlapping regulatory revisions with time-stamped queries be built whose labels are valid evidence about real retrieval behaviour, given that existing temporal legal QA sets are LLM-synthesized (with expert validation) rather than drawn from real time-stamped user queries?
description: The only retrieved resource with version-aware statutory questions (arxiv:2605.23497) uses LLM-synthesized questions, subsequently expert-validated; TIQ is fully automatically generated. A benchmark of overlapping regulatory revisions with time-stamped queries would likely also need to be synthesized. It is unclear whether synthetic time-sensitive queries support valid claims about retrieval-ranking behaviour on real amended corpora, or whether they risk encoding the generator's own recency assumptions.
rationale: Construct validity of the planned benchmark is a precondition for any claim that a soft temporal score improves answer accuracy; if synthetic queries encode recency assumptions, the main result could be circular.
